title: Redpanda Pricing: Plans and Costs Explained (2026)
summary: Redpanda pricing options vary significantly based on your deployment model and throughput needs. Use these details to select the most cost-effective tier.
body_markdown:
## Redpanda pricing plans and core features


### The free Community Edition vs. Serverless tier


By using the Community Edition, developers can run Redpanda on local hardware or self-managed containers under a source-available license. This eliminates licensing fees but shifts the entire operational burden of patching and scaling to you.


The Community Edition enforces a dual-constraint ceiling to separate free usage from enterprise scale. Users are limited to a **maximum of 50 CPU cores** across their deployment, but they must also adhere to a 3-node cluster limit.


This means you cannot bypass the core limit by spreading a small number of cores across a massive distributed fleet.


When teams move to the cloud without managing infrastructure, the Serverless tier offers a consumption-based model where you pay only for the data you ingest and store. This tier removes the need for a minimum cluster size.


It's a viable entry point for[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) users or those running lightweight event-driven workflows that don't justify a dedicated environment. Once throughput becomes consistent and high, the variable costs of the Serverless tier can quickly exceed the predictable monthly rate of a fixed cluster.


### Dedicated Cloud and BYOC pricing benchmarks


Managed by Redpanda on AWS or Google Cloud, the Dedicated Cloud tier provides a fully managed cluster service. Redpanda handles the infrastructure, but this convenience comes with a **mandatory minimum spend** that can be prohibitive for testing environments.


The Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) model deploys the Redpanda data plane into your own VPC while keeping the control plane managed by Redpanda.


This architecture allows companies to use their existing cloud provider discounts and maintain perimeter security. It requires a more complex initial setup than the standard Dedicated offering.


### The 2025 Redpanda pricing comparison table


The following table outlines the trade-offs between self-management and Redpanda's various cloud tiers, highlighting how SLAs and throughput caps scale alongside cost.

As data volume grows, the cost shifts from human operational hours to direct licensing and management fees through this progression from free local development to high-availability enterprise tiers.


### Serverless pricing versus dedicated production costs


The Serverless tier begins at a $0 base fee, charging roughly **$0.08 per GB of ingress** , which appeals to developers testing the waters by removing the financial risk of initial experimentation.


However, moving to a Dedicated production environment introduces a significant jump to a monthly minimum near $1,000, forcing teams to commit to a substantial recurring expense before scaling. This baseline covers the management of a three-node high-availability cluster and basic support.


The Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) tier typically requires an **annual commitment starting at $15,000** to $20,000 per year. While this sounds higher, it often results in a lower total bill for high-throughput users because it strips away the cloud infrastructure markup.


Organizations must weigh these fixed entry points against their projected data growth to avoid overpaying for idle capacity.
